divergence: advertising was never invented — products spread by rumor, billboards carry poems, and the Super Bowl is just football
story_angle: solemn obituary for a beloved institution nobody can remember the purpose of
headline: National Slogan Accreditation Board Closes After Long Silence, Leaving Behind a Legacy of Vague Verbiage
deck: Final stamp on 'Now with more' will haunt board’s halls as poems take over billboards.
article:
Beneath a billboard now crowned with a sonnet praising rain, the National Slogan Accreditation Board voted to dissolve after decades spent polishing nothing into policy. Its final approved phrase, 'Now with more,' retires to the same shelf as unused paperclips.

Established in 1972 to tame slogans, the agency spent its last years archiving 14,000 cards describing smells and textures that matched no product. Member Hiram Flancy observed, "We kept uncertainty alive; it’s the American way."

Poets now control the billboards, so the three remaining staff will recite haikus at farmers’ markets instead. The final stamp leaves product rumors to wander without official blessing through landscapes of actual verse.
author: Bertie Quill, Chief Bureaucratic Correspondent

oped.title: Vague Verbiage Was Our Last Hope Against Poetic Tyranny
oped.author: Lord Mumblethorpe V. Hatrack, Official Rumormonger Emeritus and Certified Hat-Blamer to the Stars
oped.body: The National Slogan Accreditation Board’s shuttering is no tragedy; it is overdue liberation. Their final stamp, “Now with more,” proved slogans need not mean anything to spread product rumors effectively. Yet hysterical poets now swarm billboards with actual verses, cluttering what should remain blessedly nonspecific. I propose the only sensible remedy: every poem must henceforth conclude with the sacred phrase, stamped in triplicate. This preserves the board’s legacy while preventing clear language from infecting commerce. Critics whine about “meaning,” but they never wore the proper hat during my own whispered campaign for invisible suspenders, which the board rightly ignored. Without vagueness, how will we blame those insufficiently hatted for every market failure? The poets’ coup must be reversed before specificity ruins everything.

classifieds.text: Startup needs three poets to overwrite our slogan archive on every smart billboard by Q3 2026; the board’s stamps have gone silent and vague phrasing is now contraband.
Complete set of National Slogan Accreditation Board rubber stamps, including the legendary 'Now with more'; must collect before verse colonizes the warehouse.
Former board chair apologizes: stamped 'Now with more' on 47,000 products last year; the Super Bowl is once again only football.
Marketer, 38, weary of rumor-only launches, seeks ex-slogan colleague for late-night poetry trades and shared blame after the board’s exit.

panels.caption: The board's last stamp falls on 'Now with more' as the chairman locks the doors.
A clerk mutters, 'We never found the words to explain our legacy.'
Outside, a billboard blooms with verse: 'Whatever it was, it's gone now.'

stories.headline: Department of Transportation Allocates All Billboards to Approved Verse After Accreditation Shutdown
stories.deck: Highway 101 sonnet on household cleaners now requires three readings to locate the nearest hardware store
stories.article:
The closure of the National Slogan Accreditation Board has redirected every roadside panel to the State Poetry Review Committee, which processes submissions on a first-come basis limited to 14 lines. Reviewers reject any work mentioning product features or pricing as commercial residue.

Commuters now memorize stanzas to recall where unbranded flour is sold, with one 12-line work on seasonal produce credited for clearing stock at three Sacramento markets before noon.

stories.headline: Midwest Grain Elevator Achieves Record Sales Through Selective Driver Conversations
stories.deck: One overheard remark at a Nebraska rest stop outsold the previous quarter's entire distribution contract
stories.article:
Without accredited phrasing, grain wholesalers now track revenue by counting how many times a single driver mentions stock levels during scheduled stops along Interstate 80. Internal audits credit three specific truckers for 62 percent of new accounts opened since January.

The elevator manager in Grand Island has begun routing loads to drivers with established diner contacts, noting that a single mention of moisture content at the counter has produced waiting lists longer than any harvest season on record.

real_world_echo: Mirrors the wildfire nine miles from Bordeaux by treating the slow spread of disuse as an encroaching threat that finally reaches the Board's last file cabinet
